verdicts.trueWording: whilst I enjoy GGK’s prose, it’s not a favourite of mine
verdicts.note: Display name is 'Booksblabbering || Cait❣️', 4 stars, 9 Jan 2026, 38 likes. Quote exact; the following sentence calls the prose evocative but says nothing stood out.

verdicts.trueWording: The prose is really purposeful and engaging, without being overly dense
verdicts.note: Tori Tecken, 4 stars, 25 Aug 2025, 31 likes. Quote exact and is the reviewer's second sentence, about her first GGK novel.

verdicts.trueWording: Kay uses too much flowery language without saying anything extra
verdicts.note: terpkristin, message 32, 14 Jun 2012 05:34AM, in the topic headed 'The Sword and Laser - 2012 Reads'. Quote exact; next sentence says Kay has not drawn her in as Martin does.

verdicts.trueWording: Kay is able to use language to evoke emotions & imagery
verdicts.note: Devin, message 31, 14 Jun 2012 05:17AM. Quote exact; the sentence continues that he had never imagined or conceived such imagery before, which supports the 'not previously conceived' limb.

verdicts.trueWording: Martin seems to write in HD, where Kay uses a soft filter
verdicts.note: Vance, message 2, 6 Jun 2012 08:31AM. Quote exact (page continues 'at times. Both perfect for different moods'), and the poster introduces it as 'a weird imagery'. 'Camera metaphor' is the claim author's label for HD/soft-filter, not the page's own word; the register contrast it names is supported by the preceding sentence on Kay being better with language.

verdicts.trueWording: Kay has nothing against staying in a place and meditating on it
verdicts.note: Amanda, message 6, 6 Jun 2012 09:50AM. Quote exact; the 'distinguishing' limb is supported by the message's frame that the two are very different kinds of authors and by the following contrast with Martin's action.

verdicts.trueWording: I often wish there was less of it
verdicts.note: Brok3n Engines, 'Tigana, by Guy Gavriel Kay', subtitle 'GGK in transition', 16 Apr 2025. Full sentence begins 'while I enjoy his prose', so both limbs hold. The reviewer's gender is never stated on the page; the claim's 'he' is not page-supported but carries none of the assertion.

verdicts.trueWording: a dialogue with the reader, and not just a monologue
verdicts.note: Post body, 11 May 2021, opening 'I have just been listening' to 'this year's JRR Tolkien Lecture', which supports the same-evening and 2021 limbs. The phrase is marked 'as he said', so it is Kay's own formulation, and the surrounding sentence gives leaving things to the imagination as the reason.

verdicts.trueWording: how much light an author should shed upon the workings of magic
verdicts.note: Post body: the sentence begins 'The topic that Guy settled on for the evening was that of', which supports the 'whole topic' limb; quote exact, ending 'in their books'.

verdicts.trueWording: His prose was as adjective free as it has ever been
verdicts.note: Brad, 4 stars, 5 Jul 2012, 25 likes. Quote exact and continues 'moreso', supporting the superlative limb; the immediacy limb is carried by the next clause on an immediacy born of that simplicity.

verdicts.trueWording: never saying more or less than was needed
verdicts.note: Mike, 5 stars, 11 Feb 2014, 14 likes. Quote exact, closing a sentence that calls the writing elegant and well balanced.

verdicts.trueWording: Kay subscribes to the “less is more” school of writing
verdicts.note: Veronica, 4 stars, 5 May 2019, 16 likes. Quote exact with the page's curly quotes; the contrast limb is supported by the preceding 'Whereas many writers are verbose' clause.

verdicts.trueWording: never veering near the purple prose so many of us detest
verdicts.note: Mayim de Vries, 4 stars, 15 Jun 2019, 34 likes. Quote exact, closing a sentence praising Kay's mastery of language.

verdicts.trueWording: Kay does go a bit overboard with commas
verdicts.note: Paul O’Neill, 4 stars, 6 Apr 2017, 82 likes. Quote exact; the page continues 'but this is more of a style point', which supports the 'habit of the style' limb. Listed under his 'Notable issues' heading.
